name: partial-change-set-update-before-create
description: A change set that is not applicable as a whole: its first operation updates an element its second operation creates. Nothing here is a broken reference — the missing target is in the set, only later than the operation that needs it — so the set would have to be applied in part, in the order given, to be applied at all. That is a refusal, never a partial commit and never a silent reordering. Whether the reordered set would also be *valid* is a separate question this class does not answer.

context.summary: A model that already declares the `RAM0` memory and the `IVehicleSpeed` interface, and holds no `SpeedSensorSWC`. The client wrote the description update first and the create second.

input.intent: Add the speed sensor component and set its description.

operations.value: Reads the wheel speed sensors and publishes the vehicle speed

expected.notes: The discrimination against `broken-reference` is the staged result: a broken reference is a dangling reference or an unresolvable address in the OUTCOME, while this outcome is fine and only the ordered application is not. The fix belongs to the client — put the `create` first, or fold the description into its payload — because reordering on the client's behalf would commit a sequence nobody reviewed. Applying the valid subset was considered and rejected: it produces a model state no one intended and breaks the reviewed-delta-equals-committed-delta guarantee.
